Method of Attack: Banking trojan with persistence on infected systems
Collecting sensitive information such as firewall configuration, OS info, admin privileges, antivirus status
Using false system update popups to deceive users
Taking screenshots, manipulating windows, simulating mouse and keyboard actions, restarting machine
Hijacking cryptocurrency by replacing Bitcoin wallet address in clipboard
Stealing saved passwords from Chrome browser
Disabling browser autocomplete by fiddling registry values
Passing context between processes to evade detection
Downloading payloads via chained downloaders using custom HTTP verbs and User-Agent headers
Encrypting strings with custom cryptographic algorithm
Generating dynamic C&C domains using arithmetic operations and MD5 hashes

Attack Vector: Phishing spam emails with malicious ZIP file attachments
Indicators of Compromise: Phishing emails pretending to contain receipts
URLs with custom HTTP verbs (e.g., '111SA') and custom User-Agent headers
False Windows update popups in Portuguese
Registry keys such as 'HKCU\Software\Microsoft\windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\AutoComplete\' being disabled
Dynamic C&C domains generated from fake domain lists and port lists
Use of SQL stored procedures on C&C servers instead of direct SQL queries
